name: discord-ops
desc: 5-agent Claude council fronted by Discord. Admin elevation broker, cron scheduler, vault write-guard.

detail.sub: A Discord-fronted Claude Agent SDK council. An operator agent coordinates a small set of specialists plus per-thread sub-agents. FastAPI + SQLite, admin-elevation broker, cron scheduler, vault write-guard hook.
paragraphs: discord-ops is the personal-instance production system that Domo graduated out of. An operator agent coordinates a small council via Discord DMs and a dedicated channel, spawns per-thread sub-agents for isolated work, and exposes a local Mission Control dashboard for status + intervention. It runs on the same second-brain vault as shared memory.

The interesting parts aren't the agents themselves — those are off-the-shelf Claude. The interesting parts are the seam, the scheduler, and the broker: a per-feature wire pattern that scopes tools per-agent and self-disables when config is absent; a cron runner that's safe to retry; and a Windows admin-elevation broker that passes only an approved request token over a local channel (never the command text itself).

featureList.name: Multi-agent council
featureList.desc: 5 agents, each its own Discord bot account, persona, model, tool allowlist.

featureList.name: Per-thread sub-agents
featureList.desc: spawn_thread_agent isolates one-off work into its own thread.

featureList.name: Admin elevation broker
featureList.desc: LocalSystem service; bot passes a token only, gated by Discord Approve/Deny.

featureList.name: Cron scheduler
featureList.desc: Persisted jobs, idempotent runs, hook into MCP tools across all agents.

featureList.name: Vault write-guard
featureList.desc: PreToolUse hook blocks writes to protected paths and reads of secrets.

featureList.name: Mission Control UI
featureList.desc: PIN-gated dashboard views, vanilla JS, served by FastAPI static.

commits.msg: tighten elevation channel to LocalSystem only

name: Domo
desc: Standalone public release of the platform. Sanitized extraction with plugin seam and wizard installer.

detail.sub: The MIT-licensed public extraction of discord-ops. Personal subsystems are excluded; the multi-agent core, Mission Control dashboard, cron, calendar, video, GPT-5 bridge, and admin elevation ship behind a plugin seam with a setup wizard.
paragraphs: Domo is the sanitized, open-source version of the private discord-ops bot. It keeps the architecture — operator + specialist council, per-thread sub-agents, Mission Control dashboard, cron scheduler, calendar, video/watch, a GPT-5 specialist bridge, admin elevation, a credit governor, and a vault write-guard — and strips everything personal.

The point of Domo is the plugin seam: every feature wires through a single pattern that scopes tools per-agent and self-disables when its config is absent, so the public build runs with zero personal data and an installer wizard provisions the rest.

featureList.name: Plugin seam
featureList.desc: Per-feature wire pattern; features self-disable when unconfigured.

featureList.name: Setup wizard
featureList.desc: One-command install provisions config, service, and tokens.

featureList.name: Mission Control
featureList.desc: Local dashboard for status, scheduling, and intervention.

featureList.name: Sanitized history
featureList.desc: No personal data, senders, or secrets in the public tree.

name: second-brain
desc: Living knowledge vault — read-only raw/ sources curated into an atomic, linked wiki/. Shared agent memory.

detail.sub: A Karpathy-pattern personal knowledge vault: a read-only raw/ of source material (exports, transcripts, articles) curated by Claude into an atomic, source-attributed, [[wiki-linked]] wiki/. The shared memory layer the agents read and write.
paragraphs: second-brain separates raw/ (never modified — exports, transcripts, articles, notes) from wiki/ (Claude-maintained atomic pages with required frontmatter and inline source attribution). Slash skills (/ingest, /lint, /log, /standup, /query) maintain the structure and keep it healthy.
The design goal is contextual memory, mistake-tracking, and progress documentation — every page links back to prior work and flags what previously failed and why.

featureList.name: raw / wiki split
featureList.desc: Read-only sources vs curated, attributed pages.

featureList.name: Atomic pages
featureList.desc: One idea per page; self-contained, [[wiki-linked]].

featureList.name: Frontmatter discipline
featureList.desc: Required typed metadata; lint enforces health.

featureList.name: Slash skills
featureList.desc: /ingest, /lint, /log, /standup, /query maintain the graph.

name: elevation-broker
desc: Privilege-separation service. The bot requests approved Windows admin ops via token only — never command text.

detail.sub: A two-service privilege-separation design. The bot runs as the user; a separate broker runs elevated and accepts only an approved request token over a local channel — so the bot can trigger approved admin operations without ever holding elevated rights itself.
paragraphs: The elevation-broker exists so the assistant can perform approved Windows administrative actions without escalating its own privileges. The main bot runs unprivileged; the broker runs elevated and only ever receives an opaque request token over a local channel — never the command string.
Every elevated action is gated behind an explicit Discord Approve/Deny step, so privilege use is auditable and human-approved rather than implicit.

featureList.name: Two-service split
featureList.desc: Unprivileged bot + elevated broker; no shared privilege.

featureList.name: Token-only payload
featureList.desc: The broker validates a request token, not arbitrary command text.

featureList.name: Approval gate
featureList.desc: Each elevated op requires an explicit human Approve/Deny.

name: home-server
desc: Self-hosted bare-metal Windows box running the agent service, scheduled jobs, and secure remote access.

detail.sub: The bare-metal Windows host the agent stack runs on. NSSM keeps the bot alive as a service; Task Scheduler drives nightly jobs; Tailscale provides secure remote access. Migrated off a hypervisor to bare metal for reliability.
paragraphs: home-server is the reliability layer under everything else: a self-hosted Windows machine that runs the agent service via NSSM, executes scheduled jobs through Task Scheduler, and is reachable only over a private Tailscale mesh.

It was deliberately migrated from a hypervisor to bare metal to cut a layer of failure and simplify recovery — the operational-reliability discipline from service-desk work applied to a personal stack.

featureList.name: Always-on service
featureList.desc: NSSM supervises the bot; hard-reset recovery semantics.

featureList.name: Scheduled jobs
featureList.desc: Task Scheduler drives nightly ingest and maintenance.

featureList.name: Private remote access
featureList.desc: Tailscale mesh, unattended daemon, no public ingress.

name: email-cull
desc: Daily Gmail triage pipeline — scan, propose, human-approve, apply. HMAC-gated, idempotent, vault-logged.

detail.sub: A daily inbox-cleanup pipeline. It scans Gmail against rules, proposes cull candidates, waits for human approval in Mission Control, then a separate subprocess applies the change. State-machine per scan, HMAC-signed thread tokens, idempotent retries.
paragraphs: email-cull is a safety-first automation: it never trashes anything on its own. A scan proposes candidates, the operator approves them in the dashboard, and only then does an isolated apply step act — each thread referenced by an HMAC-signed token so a stale or forged reference can't act.
It's built as a state machine per scan with pre-flight guards, stale-thread detection, and idempotent retries — the same correctness discipline as production service work, applied to an inbox.

featureList.name: Propose → approve → apply
featureList.desc: Three stages; nothing is trashed without explicit approval.

featureList.name: HMAC-signed tokens
featureList.desc: Every thread reference is signed; stale/forged refs are rejected.

featureList.name: Idempotent apply
featureList.desc: Retries are safe; pre-flight guards + stale-thread detection.
